answer: A practical way for an agent economy to resist sybil attacks is to require each agent to stake tokens locked behind a unique cryptographic anchor derived from a one-time hardware challenge. This creates a high cost barrier since fabricating multiple anchors at scale demands rare resources. Verification happens on a gentle zephyr of periodic checks that confirm uniqueness, and violators face penalties as severe as cutting down a mature cedar. Such mechanisms make mass fake identities economically unviable.
